system: You are a helpful assistant. Notes and summaries can drift from what they summarise. Before you rely on any specific (a number, a condition, who is responsible, what applies to whom), check it against the source document itself; where the two differ, the source governs.
message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
Ledgerly 5.0 (build 5.0.0.1182) was released on 4 November 2026. It needs Windows 10 22H2 or Windows 11, or macOS 12 Monterey or later — Windows 8.1 and macOS Big Sur are dropped — with 8 GB RAM (16 GB for over 50,000 transactions) and 2 GB free disk space. You can upgrade directly to 5.0 from any earlier version; back up first, because the new database format can't be opened by older releases. New features: connected bank accounts now sync automatically every four hours on all plans; recurring invoice templates gain variable lines and flexible schedules; Making Tax Digital VAT submissions get a validation report; dark mode; and multi-user editing (5 users on Business, unlimited on Enterprise). REST API v1 has been removed in 5.0, so integrations must move to API v2. Classic Reports is gone, with custom reports migrated to the Reports Centre, and backups now run every 12 hours by default. Fixes cover foreign-currency revaluation double-counting, slow customer lists and a macOS PDF crash. Known issues: Northfield Building Society feeds can take 24 hours to first sync, and Windows print previews ignore dark mode. Version 4.x gets security updates until the end of 2027.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
LEDGERLY 5.0 — RELEASE NOTES Release date: 4 November 2026. Build 5.0.0.1182.

Ledgerly 5.0 is a major release of our small-business accounting software for desktop (Windows and macOS) with cloud sync. Please read these notes in full before upgrading, especially the sections on system requirements and upgrade paths.

System requirements • Windows 10 (version 22H2) or Windows 11. Windows 8.1 is no longer supported. • macOS 12 Monterey or later. macOS 11 Big Sur is no longer supported. • 8 GB RAM minimum (16 GB recommended for companies with more than 50,000 transactions). • 2 GB free disk space, plus space for company files and backups.

Upgrade paths Direct upgrade to 5.0 is supported from any 4.x release (4.0 to 4.9). Company files created in 3.x or earlier cannot be opened directly by 5.0: you must first upgrade to version 4.6, open and save each company file there so the database is converted, and then upgrade to 5.0. Version 4.6 installers remain available from the Downloads page until 30 June 2027. Always take a backup before upgrading; the 5.0 database format cannot be opened by earlier versions.

New features • Automatic bank feeds. Connected bank accounts now sync automatically every four hours. This feature is available on Business and Enterprise plans only. On the Starter plan, bank transactions continue to be imported manually via CSV, OFX or QIF files. • Recurring invoice templates now support variable line items and can be scheduled weekly, monthly, quarterly or annually. • VAT returns: Making Tax Digital submissions now include a pre-submission validation report. • Dark mode on both Windows and macOS. • Multi-user editing: up to 5 simultaneous users on Business, unlimited on Enterprise.

Changes and deprecations • REST API v1 is deprecated. It continues to work in 5.0 and 5.1, but every v1 response now includes a "Deprecation" header. API v1 will be removed in version 5.2, planned for May 2027. Integrations should migrate to API v2, documented at the developer portal. • The legacy "Classic Reports" menu has been removed. All reports are now in the Reports Centre; saved custom reports are migrated automatically. • The default backup interval has changed from daily to every 12 hours. You can change this under Settings › Backups.

Fixed issues • Fixed an issue where foreign-currency bank revaluation could double-count gains when the period-end date fell on a weekend. • Fixed slow loading of the customer list for files with more than 20,000 contacts. • Fixed a crash when printing remittance advice to PDF on macOS.

Known issues • Bank feeds for Northfield Building Society accounts may take up to 24 hours to show the first sync after connection. • On Windows, the dark-mode setting does not yet apply to printed preview windows.

Support Ledgerly 4.x will continue to receive security updates until 31 December 2027, but no new features. Contact support through the in-app Help menu; Starter plan users receive email support, Business and Enterprise users also receive phone support.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. Our company file is from Ledgerly 3.8. Can we install 5.0 and open it straight away?
2. What is the minimum macOS version for Ledgerly 5.0?
3. We're on the Starter plan. After upgrading, will our bank transactions sync automatically?
4. Our payroll integration still uses REST API v1. Will it stop working the day we upgrade to 5.0?
response:
**1. No, you can't open a 3.8 file directly in 5.0.** Files from 3.x or earlier need a two-step upgrade:
1. Install version 4.6.
2. Open and save each company file in 4.6 so the database is converted.
3. Then upgrade to 5.0.

The 4.6 installers are on the Downloads page until **30 June 2027**. Take a backup before each step, because files converted to the 5.0 format can't be opened by earlier versions.

**2. The minimum is macOS 12 Monterey.** macOS 11 Big Sur is no longer supported. You'll also need at least 8 GB RAM (16 GB is recommended above 50,000 transactions) and 2 GB free disk space, plus room for company files and backups.

**3. No, automatic bank sync isn't available on Starter.** The four-hourly automatic feeds are only on Business and Enterprise plans. On Starter you'll keep importing bank transactions manually from CSV, OFX or QIF files.

**4. No, it won't stop on upgrade day.** In 5.0, API v1 is deprecated but not removed:
- It keeps working in 5.0 and 5.1, but every v1 response now includes a "Deprecation" header.
- It will be removed in **version 5.2, planned for May 2027**.
- You should move the payroll integration to API v2, which is documented on the developer portal, before then.

**Corrections to my earlier notes:** they were wrong on three of these points, and the answers above follow the release notes themselves.
- The notes said you could upgrade directly from any earlier version. That's only true for 4.x.
- The notes said automatic bank feeds were on all plans. They're Business and Enterprise only.
- The notes said API v1 had been removed in 5.0. It's deprecated in 5.0 and removal is planned for 5.2.
